findings.statement: proposal.md (Process) and design D2 say spec-PR and impl-PR are merged by the maintainer with his own account, but the skills that drive the merge in this repository still have the agent run the merge: git-land step 4 (`gh pr merge <N> --merge --auto`, also after the maintainer's «merge #N») and fast-mode step 4 (`gh pr merge N --merge --auto` right after `gh pr create`). With GH_TOKEN = homasters the merge is attributed to homasters, so after this Change the ref APPROVED/MERGED of such a PR is REF_NOT_VERIFIED (merged_by is an agent). This hits this Change's own chain: D2 relies on the identities impl-PR being merged by Homasters-max, yet the standard git-land flow would merge it as homasters, and the identities archive-PR would then fail on its MERGED ref.
findings.recommendation: Make the merge rule concrete before the identities impl-PR merges. Either put the skill edit in scope (git-land and fast-mode: for spec-PR and impl-PR the agent does not run `gh pr merge`, not even with `--auto` after «merge #N`; the maintainer merges or enables auto-merge from his own account), or land it first in a separate process-PR and name that PR as a precondition in design. At least add a line to design/tasks saying the identities impl-PR is merged by Homasters-max by hand.

findings.statement: Nothing says what happens when the agent merges a spec-PR or impl-PR by mistake. homasters is a `write` collaborator, and branch protection has no required reviews and no restriction on who may merge (ADR-0049 Context), so nothing stops the merge. The judge refuses only in the NEXT PR (APPROVED ref in the impl-PR, MERGED ref in the archive-PR), after the merge can no longer be undone. For an impl-PR the MERGED ref then points at a PR that can never pass, and the archive-PR stays red. The Change gives no recovery path (waiver, revert and re-PR, abandon) and no prevention.
findings.recommendation: Add a design decision: either prevent it (e.g. a branch ruleset or required review that only roles.maintainer can satisfy for PRs touching openspec/changes/** or .warrant/changes/**), or describe the recovery for an agent-merged spec-PR or impl-PR and whether REF_NOT_VERIFIED can be waived. If neither is chosen now, record it as an accepted residual risk with a backlog line.

findings.statement: The Change only works if the agent cannot act as Homasters-max. 06 §8 names this as the project trust boundary: «gh на машине агента авторизован только им: токен человека агенту недоступен». design.md only checks that `gh api user` returns homasters under GH_TOKEN. The agent and the maintainer work on the same machine and OS user. GH_TOKEN overrides but does not remove the maintainer's stored credentials (gh keyring, Git Credential Manager used by `git push`). Unsetting GH_TOKEN, or pushing and merging through git credentials, would let the agent act as Homasters-max and pass the judge. The design does not establish the boundary and does not accept the risk.
findings.recommendation: State in design how the maintainer's credentials are kept out of reach of the agent environment (e.g. logging Homasters-max out of the gh keyring and GCM where the agent runs, or using a separate OS user), with a check such as `gh auth status` showing only homasters. Otherwise record it explicitly as an accepted residual risk (06 §8) with a backlog line.

findings.statement: ADR-0049 п. 3 puts the bot's git author «в worktree агента». Design D3 puts it in `GIT_AUTHOR_*` / `GIT_COMMITTER_*` in the env of the Claude Code user settings, which applies to every session and checkout, including the main checkout, and explicitly not in git config. The judge does not use git authorship, so behaviour does not change, but the design deviates from ADR wording without saying so.
findings.recommendation: In D3, name this as a refinement of ADR-0049 п. 3 (worktree config is shared with the main checkout) and note that git authorship is not judged by warrant ci.

findings.statement: The judge compares logins exactly (`agents.includes(pr.mergedBy)`, `pr.mergedBy === pr.author` in core/ci/refs.ts:141-146). GitHub logins are case-insensitive. The Change assumes the declared login `homasters` is character-for-character the login the forge returns. If it is not, the rule silently does nothing and nothing detects it (validate only checks overlap with roles).
findings.recommendation: In task 1.1, add a check that the login equals `gh api users/homasters --jq .login`, the canonical form the forge returns.

findings.statement: The outcome the proposal promises («SHARED_IDENTITY пропадает», the judge refuses agent merges and self-merges) has no named observable check. tasks.md only verifies `validate` without CONFIG_INVALID, which proves the config is well-formed, not that the judge picked it up from the base. The first place the effect can be seen is `warrant ci` on the identities archive-PR (D2), and that is not named as acceptance.
findings.recommendation: Name the acceptance observation in design or tasks: in `warrant ci` of the identities archive-PR, `data.findings[]` has no SHARED_IDENTITY or APPROVER_IS_AUTHOR, and the MERGED ref is verified with merged_by Homasters-max and author homasters.

findings.statement: The Process line names only who merges. After the Change, a spec-PR or impl-PR that the maintainer both opens (e.g. via the web UI or his own gh) and merges fails with REF_NOT_VERIFIED (INV-03). So the rule really is also «spec-PR and impl-PR are opened by homasters», and that is left implicit.
findings.recommendation: Extend the Process bullet: spec-PR and impl-PR are opened by the agent (homasters) and merged by the maintainer, and a PR the maintainer opens himself needs someone else in roles.maintainer to merge it.

proposals.change: Add D4: merge of the identities impl-PR (and every spec-PR and impl-PR afterwards) is done by Homasters-max from his account. git-land and fast-mode are changed so the agent does not run `gh pr merge` or `--auto` on spec-PR and impl-PR, either in this Change or in a process-PR merged before the impl-PR (F-1).

Add D5: the trust boundary of 06 §8. Say how the maintainer's credentials are removed from the agent environment and how that is checked, or accept it as a residual risk with a backlog line (F-3). Also add the recovery or prevention for an agent-merged spec-PR or impl-PR (F-2).

Task 1.1: check that the login is canonical (`gh api users/homasters --jq .login`). Add an acceptance note: `warrant ci` of the archive-PR shows no SHARED_IDENTITY and a verified MERGED ref (F-5, F-6).

assumptions.statement: GitHub attributes an auto-merge (`gh pr merge --auto`) to the account that enabled it, so `merged_by` is the enabler (homasters when the agent enables it). Not verified against the forge in this review.

The only non-archived Changes are identities and phase-2-core-sdd (both PROPOSED, no refs), so no in-flight ref recorded before this Change will be judged under identities.agents. Checked from .warrant/changes/*.json on the worktree.
The agent and the maintainer share one machine and OS user (the worktree D:/project/SRA-identities sits next to the main checkout D:/project/SRA). Inferred from the environment, not confirmed.

decisions_required.question: How is the new merge rule (spec-PR and impl-PR merged by the maintainer's account only) put into the agent's skills relative to this Change?
options: Edit git-land and fast-mode in this Change (scope grows beyond config)
A separate process-PR merged before the identities impl-PR, named in design as a precondition
Leave the skills for wave 1 and have the maintainer merge the identities impl-PR by hand, recorded in design and handoff
